paragraphs.text: Mark things on a picture and look at the picture: a DeepSeek Harness plugin that turns an image into
a record of numbered marks, with coordinate-labelled close-ups and comparison sheets you can check.
# dsh-vision-reasoner

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that lets a model put numbered marks on a picture and
look at what it drew

. A place is named in the picture's own pixels, read off a
labelled grid, so nothing is converted fr

om a preview and no call has to be
expressed in the terms of an earlier one. It is not specific to a

ny kind of
picture: counting the people in a photograph is one use, checking which of two
similar re
gions a note meant is another.
## Tools
| Tool | Purpose |
| `camera_reset` | Point the camera at the whole picture — one square window holding all of it, the

picture drawn inside and the rest black — and see it. |
| `camera_move` | `step: "next"` walks the s
weep in reading order, `"previous"` steps back, a direction steps one whole window, and `to: [x, y]`

centres the window on a place read off the grid. |
| `camera_zoom_in` / `camera_zoom_out` | One ×2
or ÷2 step each, about the centre, `times` for several at once. The camera stays where it is left. |
| `mark_add` | Mark places by their coordinates, `at: [x, y]` in original pixels, with a radius `r`

, a caption and a colour. The camera moves to the batch and the answer is a window around it. |
| `m

ark_remove` | Delete marks by number, e.g. `[3, 7]`, when a mark is in the wrong place. |
| `mark_ed
it` | Move, resize, recaption or recolour marks by number, in one call. |

Every picture comes back with a grid whose lines sit at round positions in the
picture's own pixels

— 100, 200, 500, depending on how closely it is being looked
at — and every line is labelled with th

at number along all four edges. A number the
model reads is a number it can use. Every result also l

ists the whole record, with
the coordinates of every mark, so a mark placed twice, or in the wrong s

pot, is
visible in the next answer rather than several calls later. The tools never count
or judge w
hat is in a picture: that is the model's statement to make.

The package also publishes a skill, `vision-sweep-count`: the workflow this tool set was
built aroun

d — see the whole picture, sweep it window by window, mark as you read, read the
window that comes b

ack, count the record. A model reads a skill when a task matches one, which
matters here because poi
nting inside reasoning is a mode a model does not enter on its own.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Or from the Web UI: **Plugins → Add plugin**, with the package name. The package
declares `dsh.bundl

e.patch` → `./cordis.patch.yml` (one Host row), which the
profile loader applies the next time the p

rofile loads. There is no build step and
no install script.

The only dependency is `sharp` (Apache-2.0),
which the harness already uses for every image a sessio

n attaches
(`@deepseek-ai/dsh-attachment-local` depends on it), so a deployment that can run
this pl

ugin already has it. Nothing third-party is vendored: the icon and the two
locale files are this pac
## How it is used

1. **Look first.** A place is named from what has been seen, and the tool
descriptions say so before

anything else. The grid on the returned picture is
the only ruler: the picture is not cropped with

another tool, and no position is
read off another view of it, whose pixels are a different size.
2.

**Read the labels.** The lines are at round numbers of original pixels, so a
position is read by nam

ing the line before a feature and estimating the gap —
about a quarter of a step is as fine as the e

ye goes, which is why the grid steps
finer as the view gets closer.
3. **Mark the coordinates.** `ma

rk_add` takes `at: [x, y]`, a radius `r` in the
picture's own pixels, a caption and a colour. The ca

mera moves to what was marked
and the answer is a square window around those marks, with a cross at

each centre
and the record beside it.
4. **Sweep in windows you keep.** `camera_zoom_in` until a fac

e is big enough to read,
then walk the picture with `camera_move` and `step: "next"`: the windows ti

le the
picture from its centre, "next" goes left to right and then down, and every result
says how f

ar the sweep has got and which windows are left. A place read in a window
already used is comparable

with the last one.
5. **Check, then correct.** The marks are drawn in every view, so what is left u

nmarked
in the window in front of you is what you have not dealt with, and the record beside
it show

s a number twice or a ring on nothing. `mark_edit` moves a mark that is nearly
right and `mark_remov

e` deletes one that is not — at once, since a change comes back
as a window around what it touched a
nd a wrong ring misleads every view after it.
## Behaviour

**The record is not written to disk.** Marks live in the session log. The harness
logs every tool ca

ll with its arguments and its result, and the record is a fold of
[该节后续省略]
## Limitations

- **A mark is where the caller said it was.** The grid makes a position readable to
about a quarter

of its step, and nothing more; a mark placed from the whole
picture of a large photograph lands with

in tens of pixels, not within one.
- **A record belongs to the session that made it.** A subagent se

es the marks of
the session it was forked from; its parent does not see the subagent's. Two
agents n

eed one session to share a record.
- **Labels need a font.** Text is rendered by librsvg, so a machi

ne with no fonts
draws shapes but no digits.
- **Text width is estimated**, not measured, so a capti

on may be cut a character
early. It never overflows its tile.
- **A call that produced no result** —

a process killed mid-call — is left out of
the replayed record. The model may have been told about

a mark the replay does
not have.
- **A log written before this redesign does not replay.** Its calls

carry cell names
where the arguments now hold coordinates, so the replay reports that it could not

place them.
- **Native presentation only.** Under code execution (PTC) the calls are not logged
as `

tool/call`, so the fold does not see them.
- **Checking is cheap, not automatic.** Nothing forces a

second look, and the ledger only
reports where the camera has been: it says nothing about what a rec

and the ledger only
reports where the camera has been: it says nothing about what a rectangle holds.
